newsitem.title: CHINA: North China coal mine blast kills 91.
newsitem.headline: North China coal mine blast kills 91.

text.p: A huge gas explosion at a coal mine in northern China has killed 91 people and the death toll could climb further, officials said on Tuesday.
The huge blast created a shockwave that injured one person above ground, an official of the rescue centre for the mine at Guojiayao in Shanxi province said by telephone.
Rescue workers had recovered 91 bodies from the ruins of the coal mine since the explosion at midday on November 27, he said.
A search was under way for those still missing, the official said, adding that it was not known how many miners had been underground at the time of the blast in the mine.
"There is no hope of finding survivors," he said.
The cause of the explosion was under investigation, he said.
"We have not yet established who is responsible," he added.
Annual production in 1995 at the mine in China's largest coal producing province was 500,000 tonnes, he said.
Coal mine accidents kill about 10,000 people in China each year, many of them in smaller, poorly-organised mines run by local governments or townships.
China has passed regulations in recent years to try to reassert control over the growing number of small, unregulated mines, and to reduce deadly accidents.
